title: NOCTI Biotechnology 4275: Knowledge of Biotechnology - Biotechnology - Key milestones and pioneering scientists
subject: Biotechnology

questions.q: The dawn of the modern antibiotic era was catalyzed in 1928 by a fortuitous accident. A mold spore contaminated an open *Staphylococcus* agar plate, resulting in a clear zone where the bacteria were inhibited from growing. Which pioneering scientist is credited with this observation and the subsequent discovery of penicillin?
questions.explain: **Alexander Fleming** was a Scottish researcher who returned from vacation in 1928 to find that a *Penicillium* mold had contaminated his bacterial culture plates and was actively killing the *Staphylococcus* colonies. This serendipitous discovery led to the mass production of penicillin (the world's first true antibiotic), profoundly shaping human medicine and early biotechnology.

questions.q: In 1973, researchers Stanley Cohen and Herbert Boyer achieved a monumental milestone that essentially launched the modern biotechnology industry. Which of the following accurately describes their revolutionary breakthrough?
options: They successfully cloned the first adult mammal (Dolly the sheep) using somatic cell nuclear transfer.
They constructed the first functional recombinant DNA molecule by splicing an amphibian gene into a bacterial plasmid.
They completed the first fully automated draft sequence of the human genome.
They discovered and mapped the CRISPR-Cas9 adaptive immune system in *Streptococcus pyogenes*.
questions.explain:
Cohen and Boyer are recognized as the fathers of genetic engineering. 

In 1973, they used newly discovered restriction enzymes (EcoRI) and DNA ligase to cut a ribosomal RNA gene out of a frog (*Xenopus*) and paste it into a bacterial plasmid. They then inserted this plasmid into *E. coli*, successfully creating the very first functional **recombinant DNA (rDNA) organism**. 
> Option 'a' was Ian Wilmut (1996). 
> Option 'c' was the Human Genome Project (2001). 
> Option 'd' relates to Doudna and Charpentier (2012).

questions.q: Which scientist was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for conceptualizing the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) in 1983—a breakthrough that transformed molecular biology from a slow, painstaking process into a fast, exponential amplification system?
questions.explain:
**Kary Mullis** conceived the idea for the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) while working at the Cetus Corporation in 1983. 

His realization that repeated cycles of heating and cooling in the presence of primers and a polymerase could exponentially amplify targeted DNA segments revolutionized DNA fingerprinting, diagnostics, and genetic cloning. 
> Sanger (Option 'a') invented DNA sequencing. 
> Franklin (Option 'b') provided X-ray crystallography of DNA. 
> McClintock (Option 'c') discovered transposons ("jumping genes").
